text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mostly firmer but persistent broker selling pressured the spot August contract which lost $1.30 to close at $324.80 per tonne. October added 20 cents to close at $316.80 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York settled weaker but off the lows as trade buying stymied early losses. July lost 8 points to close at 11.37 cents/lb, while October gave up 6 points to close at 11.25 cents/lb. July is expected to remain under speculative selling pressure as speculators still hold heavy net long positions. Liquidation of the front month is expected to accelerate once July options expire on Friday.

EUROPE - West European sugar beet areas reported rains of between 6 to 25 mm in nearly all locations during the week ended June 10. Rains continued to improve low soil moisture supplies in Italy and continued to exceed normal levels by a considerable amount in Spain where yields are on the increase. The main area of concern is in eastern Germany where well below normal rains have led to developing moisture shortages in nearly half of the sugar beet area. Also in France it could be getting too dry. However, rains are expected to increase which could avert moisture stress.

The Eastern European sugar beet areas received widespread rains of between 12 to 50 mm in the second consecutive week. The rains continued to rebuild soil moisture supplies across the region and most areas have now adequate moisture aiding crop development. Agricultural sources said that crop prospects are now slightly above average. The sugar beet areas in the former Soviet Union had rains of between 12 and 50 mm in about half of the belt. Soil moisture is adequate in most areas for good early growth.

JAPAN - Sugar imports jumped in April 1997 to 206,209 tonnes, raw value, up from 69,821 tonnes imported in March and also above the April 1996 figure of 165,490 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 958,415 tonnes against 979,943 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.681 million tonnes compared to 1.716 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 450,542 tonnes raws against 453,446 tonnes, Thailand with 243,125 tonnes compared to 390,804 tonnes and South Africa with 114,542 tonnes compared to 129,768 tonnes.

Sugar exports in October/April 1996/97 amounted to 5,829 tonnes, up from 1,521 tonnes in 1995/96. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were China with 2,739 tonnes whites and Hong Kong with 2,366 tonnes.

NEW ZEALAND - Sugar imports in January/April 1997 amounted to 49,306 tonnes, down from 70,686 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached the record high of 263,774 tonnes compared to 210,379 tonnes in 1995. The major country of origin in January/April 1997 was Australia with 38,843 tonnes raws against 55,991 tonnes and 9,429 tonnes whites against 13,438 tonnes. Sugar exports in January/April 1997 reached 5,365 tonnes, slightly up on the 5,038 tonnes of 1996.

DENMARK - Sugar exports in March 1997 reached 9,727 tonnes, raw value, down from 14,211 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 77,952 tonnes compared to 82,449 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 173,004 tonnes compared to 199,559 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Norway 45,315 tonnes whites against 57,690 tonnes, Libya with 15,400 tonnes compared to nil and Iceland with 4,523 tonnes, up from 4,077 tonnes.

Sugar imports in October/March 1996/97 reached 21,862 tonnes compared to 3,768 tonnes in 1995/96. Major suppliers in 1996/97 were Germany with 11,292 tonnes whites against 2,982 tonnes and Sweden with 8,113 tonnes compared to 22 tonnes.
Bangladesh bought 25,000 tonnes of June/July white sugar at $338.75 per tonne. Iraq bought 12,000 tonnes Brazilian white sugar at $379 per tonne c&f as part of the oil-for-food programme.
